title: Jamie & Olive — 1:1 sync brief (API / Console / Dedicated / Private)
content:
Goal: align on short-term runway for API throughput, console rollout timing, Dedicated capacity commitments, and next steps for Private onboarding. Quick wins to unblock Q2 launch.

Top priorities to touch on (10–12 mins):
- API perf and cost: recent heatmap shows token-cost spike on long-context chat paths (seq > 8k). Need proposal for quantized variant A/B (q4) or prefix caching heuristics.
- Console rollout: Beta cohort of 6 customers; one reported that rollout UI shows stale model versions on refresh. Investigate if the config cache TTL differs between hosted and dedicated.
- Dedicated capacity buys: legal wants an SLAs appendix for the 3-month pilot. Confirm whether we ship with burst mode enabled by default.
- Private onboarding: customer wants on-prem installer for RHEL 9 and HSM integration. Status of infra ops checklist?
- Fallback ladder: confirm policy order (primary hosted -> regional dedicated -> private-local) and whether we expose override to customers.

Talking points / data to bring:
- Token egress by endpoint (last 7 days) + p90 latency for infer/generate/chat. (I will bring the CSV snapshot)
- Cost delta for int8 quantized v unquantized for our top-5 models.
- Small repro of console model TTL bug (steps + screenshots).

Unresolved questions I want Olive's read on:
1) If we enforce a stricter SLO for p99 <= 300ms on short prompts, are we comfortable with a policy that redirects long-context requests to a dedicated plan? (Pros: keeps p99 low. Cons: UX complexity.)
2) For Dedicated pilot, is the ops handoff checkpoint at week 2 or week 4? I heard different answers from infra and solutions eng.
3) Private deploy: do we commit to supporting customer-managed KMS or require Redwood KMS for the initial release?

Proposed decisions to land in this 1:1: (if Olive OK)
- Short-term: enable prefix/KV caching by default for chat endpoints; expose an escape hatch in console for advanced customers.
- Dedicated pilot: ship with burst mode off, but enable as opt-in after a capacity review. Legal appendix will state burst as opt-in.
- Private onboarding: require Redwood KMS for GA, support customer-managed KMS as P1 post-GA.

Action items (clear, owner, due):
- Jamie: attach 7-day token egress CSV + perf p90 chart to this doc and drop into the 1:1 Slack thread (due: 2026-03-03)
- Olive: sync with infra on cache TTL discrepancy and send short note on root cause (due: 2026-03-05)
- Ran (infra): verify if config cache is served from CDN edge vs control plane and propose fix (due: 2026-03-04)
- Solutions Eng: draft the Dedicated SLA appendix (first pass) and share link in #customer-success (owner: Priya, due: 2026-03-10)
- Jamie + Olive: finalize fallback ladder wording for console docs and make a tiny UX mock for override toggle (due: 2026-03-08)

Notes to self / talking script:
- Start with the cost/latency chart — high signal, objective.
- Say: "If we prefer predictable p99, we should accept some UX friction (redirect/plan bump) vs risking 10–20% customer regressions."
- Ask Olive whether we need an explicit opt-in experiment for redirect behavior or if gradual rollout via feature flag is enough.

Quick wins I plan to propose:
- One-line console copy: "Model version list is eventual; refresh to force update" — temp fix until TTL is fixed.
- Small infra tweak: lower cache TTL on model metadata to 30s for beta cohort.

Follow-up cadence:
- If we land decisions, plan a 15-min sync next Tuesday strictly to close action items and verify infra fixes.

Thread tags / labels for later filing: api/perf, console/bug, dedicated/pilot, private/onprem, action-items

End of brief. Keep the meeting focused to 25 mins max. If we run over, move backlogged items (billing cap, compliance checklist) to next slot.
